title: Perfect-algebra coinduction is tensor with its algebra-valued dual
statement:
Let $R\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Work in the ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], or equivalently on one-object ringed sites, with derived Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Assume that $B[0]$ is perfect over $R$, that is, isomorphic in $D(R)$ to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Write $C_B(K)\in D(B)$ for derived coinduction: if $K\to I$ is a K-injective resolution of $R$-complexes, it is represented by $\operatorname{Hom}_R(B,I)$ with $(b\cdot h)(b')=h(b'b)$. Put $D_B=C_B(R[0])$. There is a natural isomorphism in $D(B)$
$$K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D_B\xrightarrow{\sim}C_B(K)\qquad(K\in D(R)),$$
where tensor with the $B$-complex $D_B$ is [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. The comparison is adjoint to the map from the scalar restriction of $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D_B$ to $K$ obtained by tensoring $K$ with the evaluation counit $D_B\to R[0]$, $h\mapsto h(1)$. Thus its scalar restriction is the usual perfect-complex evaluation comparison $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(B,R)\to R\operatorname{Hom}_R(B,K)$. No boundedness of $K$, flatness of $B$ over $R$, or Noetherianity is required.

source.place: Tag 0BZE (lemma-RHom-is-tensor-special), with the evaluation-normalized comparison of trivial duality, Tags 0A70 and 0A71.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction]. For arbitrary $K$ it supplies $C_B(K)$, $U C_B(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(B,K)$, the adjunction $U\dashv C_B$, and its evaluation-at-$1$ counit. In particular $D_B=C_B(R[0])$ is a genuine object of $D(B)$; to identify the comparison required in the statement we will exhibit a $B$-linear representative whose counit composite is tensor evaluation.

source.place: Tags 0A70 and 0A71, ordinary unbounded coinduction adjunction and its scalar restriction

proof.text: Choose a complex representing $K$ and a K-flat resolution $F$ of it by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], specialized to the small one-object ringed site. Choose K-injective resolutions $R[0]\to J$ and $q:F\otimes_R J\to I$ using [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Since $F$ is K-flat, $F\to F\otimes_R J$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]; thus $I$ represents $K$. Set $V=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(B,J)$ with its coinduction $B$-action. By Step 1, $V$ represents $D_B$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(B,I)$ represents $C_B(K)$. By [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], $F\otimes_R V$ represents $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D_B$, even though $V$ need not be K-flat.

source.place: Tags 06YS and 0A94; K-flat and K-injective resolutions, specialized to ordinary modules

proof.text: Define $t:F\otimes_R V\to\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(B,I)$ by $t(f\otimes h)(b)=q(f\otimes h(b))$. This is balanced and $B$-linear: $t(f\otimes bh)(b')=q(f\otimes h(b'b))=(b\,t(f\otimes h))(b')$. For homogeneous $f$ of degree $a$, the differential of its value is $q(df\otimes h(b)+(-1)^a f\otimes dh(b))$, exactly the total-tensor differential; there is no contribution from $d_B$ since $B$ is in degree zero. Evaluation at $1$ gives $q(f\otimes h(1))$. Hence under Step 2's identifications its counit composite is precisely tensoring $K$ with $D_B\to R[0]$. By the adjunction in [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction], $Qt$ is the comparison specified in the item. Forgetting the $B$-action leaves the usual Hom/tensor evaluation comparison, with the same formula and these K-flat/K-injective models.

source.place: Tags 0A70 and 0A71; explicit verification of evaluation normalization

proof.text: By [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], choose a bounded complex $P$ of finitely generated projective $R$-modules with $QP\simeq B[0]$. Since $P$ is bounded above and projective, [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] realizes this isomorphism by a chain map $p:P\to B[0]$. Its localization is an isomorphism, so it induces isomorphisms on every cohomology module and is a quasi-isomorphism, using [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. This construction gives an actual map for precomposition below; no $B$-action or algebra structure on $P$ is needed.

source.place: Perfect complexes and Tag 0A66 (projective source Hom); derived.tex Tag 05RT for the cohomology criterion

proof.text: For any complex $N$, put $D=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,R[0])$. The degreewise normalized isomorphisms of [lem-pc-perfect-ring-hom-tensor-degrees] assemble to a chain isomorphism $A_N:D\otimes N\simeq\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_R(P,N)$ by [lem-pc-perfect-ring-hom-tensor-differential]. Thus the composite $F\otimes\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)\xrightarrow{1\otimes A_N^{-1}}F\otimes D\otimes N\xrightarrow{\text{symmetry}}D\otimes F\otimes N\xrightarrow{A_{F\otimes N}}\operatorname{Hom}(P,F\otimes N)$ is a chain isomorphism. It is exactly $e(f\otimes h)(x)=f\otimes h(x)$: for degrees $|f|=a,|\lambda|=r,|n|=s$, the symmetry and final normalization give $(-1)^{ar+r(a+s)}=(-1)^{rs}$, the input normalization of $A_N(\lambda\otimes n)$. Boundedness and finite projectivity are used only for $P$; no bound on $F,N$ is used. This is a direct composition of the two cited normalized statements, not an assertion that an arbitrary tensor-Hom isomorphism is evaluation.

source.place: Tag 0ATK, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism, case (1); explicit normalized finite-projective calculation

proof.text: Precomposition with $p$ gives a square with top $t$, bottom $\operatorname{Hom}(P,q)\circ e$ for $N=J$, left vertical $1_F\otimes p^*:F\otimes\operatorname{Hom}(B,J)\to F\otimes\operatorname{Hom}(P,J)$, and right vertical $p^*:\operatorname{Hom}(B,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}(P,I)$. The square commutes: both composites evaluate on $f,h,x$ to $q(f\otimes h(p(x)))$. Both $p^*$ maps are quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined], with identity as its K-injective-target comparison and $p$ as its source quasi-isomorphism. Tensoring the first with $F$ preserves that property by [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. The bottom map is a quasi-isomorphism: $e$ is an isomorphism by Step 5, and $\operatorname{Hom}(P,q)$ is one by the canonical, covariantly natural Hom model of [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model], since $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $P$ is bounded above projective. On cohomology the two vertical maps and bottom map are isomorphisms, so commutativity implies that $t$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Its underlying $R$-map is therefore an isomorphism in $D(R)$, and conservativity in [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] makes $Qt$ an isomorphism in $D(B)$.

source.place: Tag 0A66 and Tag 0ATK case (1); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0A95 for precomposition into K-injectives

proof.text: The comparison is natural and independent of these resolutions because it is the adjunct of the canonical tensor-counit map, by Step 3. More explicitly, for $u:K\to K'$ in $D(R)$, the two naturality composites have the same adjunct $u\circ(1_K\otimes\epsilon_R)$, by functoriality of tensor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] and the adjunction [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction]; its Hom bijection therefore makes them equal. The formula in Step 3 identifies the underlying scalar comparison with ordinary perfect evaluation, proving the final clause as well. Only $P$ was bounded and finite projective. The complexes representing $K$, its K-flat resolution, and its K-injective replacement were arbitrary unbounded complexes; neither flatness of $B/R$ nor Noetherianity was used.

source.place: Tag 0BZE and Tags 0A70, 0A71; naturality of the evaluation-normalized comparison

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BZE, proved here by explicit ordinary-projective evaluation instead of the source's DG resolution argument; uses Tags 0A70, 0A71, more-algebra.tex Tags 0A66 and 0ATK, and the cited normalized chain calculations.
